analysis.title: GS McGeoch - Copper and Gold Traders thoughts and Chile Labour considerations...Three buckets of ask and we still favour upside in GSXGCOPP
key_insights: The desk still favours upside in copper via a GSXGCOPP Jan27 110%/130% call spread that costs 3.5% for 26 days, a 5.7x pay-out.

Copper has lacked follow-through buying because the market thinks it is at peak tightness today. The desk argues the forward view may not support that, and that only one of three buckets needs to hold: demand recovers, tariffs stay on, or supply issues persist.
China is absorbing macro copper selling. The desk thinks physical strength will stop out AI capex-related shorts.

Shanghai saw modest spec short-covering overnight. Social plus bonded inventory fell 4k t vs Monday and is down 69% y/y. The spot premium (customs cleared) rose to CNY 2,100/mt, supporting the cash arb, and Nov/Dec SHFE at CNY 1,490 is helping open the Nov26 arb.

The US export arb from Long Beach to China is opening on CIF premium strength (last $200/mt) and a negative prompt CME arb. The desk does not think this ends the bull thesis that the US absorbs the global surplus. It cites only ~20k MT in Long Beach, most metal sitting in New Orleans where the export arb is closed, and metal leaving only because China is tight.
The desk expects the administration to take a dim view of rising US copper exports.
Franchise copper flow is low. The desk's impression is that macro funds are short on rates and AI capex views but reluctant to add given China physical tightness.
Copper vol is still bid after post-LME put buying. The desk thinks the risky bid to puts is wrong given China physical and is looking to sell it.
Gold is rallying on CTA covering and modest Chinese buying. The desk has not seen significant macro engagement.

A macro take from Privo frames gold as an inverse oil trade: EM central banks tapped reserves or stopped buying when energy bills rose, and as oil reverses, funding pressure eases and gold catches a bid. Long gold may be a more defensible de-escalation trade than short oil.

China has covered shorts on SHFE and is starting to add modest length, but the desk sees no re-engagement from its franchise. Twice this year option length reached ~50% of Jan27 highs and price gave up both times on rates and oil.
The desk's CTA model is close to max short in gold, and it sees the pain trade as higher.
GLD plus iShares ETF local VWAP is ~$4,400. GLD had its first monthly outflow since June (-$1.8bn), nearly reversing September's inflows.
Chile copper labour negotiations add a supply risk into 2027 (per the GIR note). They matter most for BHP, RIO, LUN and ANTO.
Equity flow has been mostly two-way in GLEN. The desk says it is better to buy FCX on Tuesday, not Wednesday, and LUN ahead of its print. US and EU pads saw more energy than materials flow.

The desk gets many asks on what price can be underwritten in IVN, and notes the capital intensity of new vs the value of installed assets after the FCX update. It recalls the BHP comment at the GS LME conference: 'buy and build rather than buy vs. build'.
The market will keep a soft eye on the Argentina elections in a year.

market_movers.rationale: Greatest exposure to Chile labour risk via Escondida and Spence (GSe ~75% of copper production). Escondida has a history of industrial action.
Exposed to Chile labour talks through Escondida (~35% of copper production).
Lundin Mining (LUN) is exposed through Caserones (~40% of copper production). Caserones has a history of industrial action.
Antofagasta (ANTO) is exposed through Los Pelambres (~55%) and Centinela (~30%). The recent Centinela strike is a precedent, though the Los Pelambres talks are with a smaller union.
The desk says it is better to buy FCX on Tuesday rather than Wednesday.

sector_views.rationale: The desk favours upside in copper. Chinese physical tightness, tariffs and supply risks such as Chile labour support it.

earnings_insights: LUN: the desk suggests buying ahead of the print and notes the post-print period has been quiet. No EPS or revenue figures are given.

risk_factors: Chile copper labour negotiations add supply risk into 2027, with Escondida and Caserones having a history of industrial action.
An open US export arb could reduce US absorption of surplus copper, and the administration may oppose rising exports.
Gold rallies have faded twice this year on rates and oil, and the desk finds it hard to add meaningful risk in November.
The market may keep treating copper as at peak tightness, limiting follow-through buying.
Macro funds are short copper on rates and AI capex views.
vol_and_positioning: Copper vol is still bid after post-LME put buying. The desk thinks the risky bid to puts is wrong given China physical and is looking to sell it.
Franchise copper flow is low. Macro funds are thought to be short on rates and AI capex but reluctant to add.
Gold option length reached ~50% of Jan27 highs twice this year, and price gave up both times on rates and oil. The desk was also too long and added convexity into FOMC.
The desk's gold CTA model is close to max short, so the pain trade is likely higher.
GLD plus iShares ETF local VWAP is ~$4,400.
geopolitical: US tariffs on copper staying on is one of the three supply-demand buckets the desk cites.
The administration is expected to take a dim view of rising US copper exports.
Oil reversing on de-escalation is cited in the Privo take as easing funding pressure on EM central bank gold holders.
Argentina elections in one year are on the market's radar for 2027.
cross_bank_references: Reference to the GS GIR note 'Chile Copper: Labour Negotiations Add Another Supply Risk Into 2027'.
